key_insight: DFT predicts that lead-free double perovskites K/Rb2SnGeX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) are stable, ductile, and strongly tunable in bandgap and thermoelectric performance through halogen substitution.
engineering_relevance: These materials could serve as environmentally safer absorbers for photovoltaics, near-IR optoelectronics, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery devices.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) for structure, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor checks for stability
Elastic, band structure, and transport analysis across Cl/Br/I compositions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds as thermodynamically stable, direct-gap semiconductors with bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV and a peak ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: These are computational predictions only, so experimental synthesis, phase stability, defect tolerance, and device-level performance still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
